strings.SAU_THENEWORDER_DESC: From humble beginnings, the house of al-Saud became one of the dominant powers of the entire Arabian peninsula - and when World War Two changed everything, in Arabia everything stayed the same. With meetings and handshakes, the Saudi royalty kept its independence under the wings of the Italian empire - becoming the only nation in the Italian sphere not to host a garrison from Rome, all in exchange for easy access to oil. Thanks to oil deals with Italy, the Saudi house became fabulously rich, and they fully intend to put their wealth to good use. As many in the Arab and Islamic world look to Riyadh as a beacon for Muslim opposition to western imperialism, the Saudis silently bid their time, waiting for the right moment to lead the fight against the Italian oppressors, and to finally achieve their true calling as the leaders of the faithful.
strings.SAU_fascism_party_long: Munazamat ath-Thawrah al-Islamīyah fi al-Jazīrah al-'Arabīyah
strings.SAU_defenders_of_the_umma_desc: As the Custodians of the Two Holy Mosques, the house of Saud exerts a large influence on some sectors of the Muslim world. Many of the faithful, feeling oppressed by western and especially Italian imperialism, have turned to Saudi Arabia as a bulwark of Islam and resistance - leading to the creation of organizations such as the Muslim Brotherhood. While nominal allies, Italy and the Saudi kingdom are growing more and more distrustful of each other as a direct result, with relationships slowly but steadily deteriorating.
strings.SAU_salafi_ascendancy_desc: A puritanical and conservative reform movement in Islam, Salafism has been a dominant force in Saudi culture ever since the 18th century. The teachings of its founder, ibn Abd al-Wahhab, are the official, state sponsored form of Islam in the country, and Salafi clerics are an influential force in the Saudi court. In Saudi Arabia, the border between faith and politics is perhaps blurrier than in any other place on Earth.
strings.SAU_kingdom_of_black_gold_desc: Once a mere tribal state in the Arabian heartland, the Saudi state saw its fortunes rising thanks to Allah, and thanks to oil. The black gold pours from the sands in seemingly endless supply, and its importance in Saudi economy vastly overshadows that of any other sector. Thanks to their alliance with Italy, the Saudis managed to build a massive hoard of wealth by selling their oil around the world, so much money they barely know how to spend it.
strings.SAU_ARCO_ENI_memorandum_of_understanding: When Axis troops stormed the Middle East, the Saudis welcomed them with open arms - and ever since the end of World War Two, they pursued a policy of collaboration with Italy, eventually culminating in an agreement between their respective national oil companies. In a true masterpiece of trade diplomacy, the Saudis reaffirmed their alliance to Italy, while ENI agreed to a treaty of non-competition with ARCO. In exchange for some of the cash, ENI tankers sail the seas transporting Saudi oil and trade agents, and wherever they go, the influence of Riyadh follows them.
